title: Isandro and the Ember
premise: Wendell Oyelaran, last apprentice of the Thornfell Wayfinders' Guild, discovers that the ember they've carried as a guild heirloom is the sleeping heart of a forgotten god — and that the old gods are waking because someone is hunting them. Hunted by both the Crown's inquisitors and a zealot sect that wants to devour the god's power, Wendell and Isandro, an exiled priest who remembers a life he never lived, must carry the ember across the mountains to the god's ruined temple before the solstice. Along the way Wendell learns their own memories were rewritten by the guild to hide their divine parentage. In the end, Wendell chooses love over duty: rather than restore the god or destroy it, they merge with the ember, becoming something new — neither mortal nor divine — while Isandro breaks his vows to stay at their side.
about_author: Paloma Joubert is a former cartographer who spent five years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy rooted in landscapes, folklore, and the quiet cost of choosing who you want to be.

chapters.title: The Last Apprentice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Thornfell Wayfinders' Guild has dwindled to four members; Wendell guides a final paying caravan through the smuggler's roads while mourning the guild's slow death. Emotional beat: quiet grief and stubborn pride in a dying craft.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the border town of Vael's Crossing, exiled priest Isandro prays out of habit — and for the first time in three hundred years, something answers. He flees the shrine, terrified, carrying a name he doesn't recognize: Wendell Oyelaran. Beat: dread laced with longing.

chapters.title: The Ember in the Vault
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Guildmaster Sefu reveals the truth: the heirloom ember has begun to glow again, and the guild's founding charter binds them to protect it 'until the gods wake.' That night, inquisitors arrive asking questions no one should know to ask. Beat: the safe world cracks open.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The guildhouse burns; Sefu dies buying time, pressing the ember into Wendell's hands with one instruction: take it to the Hollow Temple by solstice. Wendell escapes through passages only a Wayfinder knows. Beat: loss transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro intercepts Wendell on the high road, sent by the answering voice itself. He knows the mountain paths' old names — names erased from every map. Distrust flares between them, but the inquisitors' hounds force alliance. Beat: wary collision.

chapters.title: Roads That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Traveling together, Wendell realizes Isandro's 'remembered' routes match the guild's secret maps exactly — including ones Wendell has never been shown. Someone rewrote history, and both of them are living inside the lie. Beat: mounting unease.

chapters.title: The Zealot's Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Ashen Choir, a sect that devours gods, corners them; their leader, Mother Serah, offers Isandro restoration of his stolen past if he surrenders the ember. He refuses — but the offer plants a seed of doubt about what he was. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Sheltering in a cave shrine, Wendell touches the ember and glimpses a memory not their own: a woman with their face, standing before a burning temple. The ember is showing them pieces of themselves they never lived. Beat: identity begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vale
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The Crown's chief inquisitor, pragmatic and weary, explains her orders: recover the ember or the realm burns in a second Godswar. She is not cruel — she may even be right. Beat: the antagonist gains humanity and moral weight.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Greywater
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A betrayal by a caravan contact strands them mid-crossing; Isandro nearly dies holding the rope bridge, and Wendell realizes their feelings have stopped being professional. First kiss in the rain, half-drowned. Beat: love admitted under pressure.

chapters.title: Songs of the First War
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. An old hermit-singer tells the true history: the gods weren't destroyed in the Godswar — they were imprisoned by mortals, and the guild was founded as jailers. The ember isn't a relic; it's a prisoner. Beat: the mission's morality inverts.

chapters.title: Sefu's Letters
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Among Sefu's effects, Wendell finds letters revealing the guild deliberately erased Wendell's childhood memories after finding them as an infant at the Hollow Temple — the god's child, hidden in plain sight. Beat: betrayal by everyone they trusted.

chapters.title: Running from Yourself
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Shattered, Wendell tries to abandon the ember and flee alone; Isandro follows and forces the confrontation Wendell has been avoiding: you cannot outrun what you are. They fight, then grieve, then choose each other properly. Beat: dark night of the soul.

chapters.title: The Choir Closes In
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The Ashen Choir sacrifices a captured god-fragment to accelerate their hunt, gaining the ability to smell the ember. Serah's conviction is absolute: a world without gods is a world without masters. Beat: the threat becomes unstoppable.

chapters.title: Vale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Vale catches up and offers Wendell sanctuary for the ember in the Crown's vaults — protection, but another cage. Wendell counters: help us reach the temple, and the gods' fate will be decided openly, not buried again. Uneasy truce. Beat: enemies negotiating.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The final ascent through the storm-wracked Pass of Teeth; the Choir ambushes, Vale's soldiers hold the line, and Vale dies covering their retreat, telling Wendell, 'Make it worth the war I didn't start.' Beat: sacrifice and grief.

chapters.title: Doors of the Hollow Temple
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the ruined temple as the solstice sun sets; the doors answer to Wendell's blood, opening onto a chamber where the god's voice finally speaks its name — and asks its child what it wants. Beat: awe and terror.

chapters.title: Serah Ascendant
chapters.summary: Serah's POV / climax part one. The Choir breaches the temple; Serah seizes the ember and begins the devouring rite, and the mountain itself starts to die as the god is unmade. Isandro holds the rite's circle with prayers he barely believes. Beat: everything failing.

chapters.title: The Choice of Embers
chapters.summary: Climax. Wendell steps into the rite and offers a third path: not restoration, not destruction, but merging — taking the god's heart into themselves, ending the war before it reignites. The god accepts. Light swallows the chamber. Beat: love against duty, resolved.

chapters.title: Neither Mortal nor Divine
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell wakes changed — able to hear prayers, bound to no heaven — and destroys the Choir's power by simply refusing to be worshipped. Serah, offered mercy, walks into exile broken. Beat: victory without triumphalism.

chapters.title: What We Carry Down
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Descent from the mountain. Isandro formally renounces his order, choosing Wendell over the vows that were built on lies about him anyway. Quiet scene: two people deciding what ordinary life looks like after miracles. Beat: tenderness.

chapters.title: The Guild Reborn
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. One year later, Wendell reopens the Wayfinders' Guild — teaching maps, mountains, and memory honestly this time — with Isandro keeping the shrine. Prayers still get answered, gently. Final line lands the theme: some things we inherit; some we choose. Beat: hopeful resolution.
